summary: A child's Medicaid ended in the post-pandemic review, likely over paperwork, and a follow-up visit cost a large share of the family's income.
realLife: Two Colorado families told NBC News about coverage lost in the post-pandemic review of Medicaid. One toddler with a heart murmur lost coverage, likely over a paperwork issue, while a sibling in the same home kept it; a single follow-up cost about $1,100 on a yearly income of roughly $35,000, and the parents waited longer before an emergency visit. A 3-year-old with autism lost home therapy when coverage ended without notice; it came back after about five months, and he stayed on a waiting list. A safety bed order arrived in December, but Medicaid no longer covered a tech add-on.
